name: BuddyWatch
title: Veteran support platform · 3 web panels
description: BuddyWatch by SixWatch is a veteran support platform with three web panels: one for the Veteran, one for the Advocate who supports them, and one for the community Partner who delivers services.

challenge.heading: Support that keeps veterans in control
paragraphs: Veterans, the peer advocates who support them and the community partners who deliver services all needed their own tools, but the work between them had to stay connected and private.
A veteran agrees before any referral is sent, recording needs its own consent, and each role sees only its own people and data.
The goal: three panels that share one shell and one vocabulary, with a crisis line visible on every screen.

rows.heading: Six roles, three journeys
rows.text: I mapped who does what: the Veteran registers, gets matched and follows a plan; the Advocate enrolls, trains, meets, plans and refers; the Partner accepts, serves and closes each referral with an outcome. Staff, command and supervisors work through those panels.
rows.caption: Partner · accept a referral

rows.heading: One shell, three panels
rows.text: Every desktop screen follows the same skeleton: sidebar, top bar, crisis notice, hero card, three stat cards and a two-column body. Only the content and vocabulary change by role.
rows.caption: Veteran · Mission Action Plan

rows.heading: Every row says what’s next
rows.text: Screens were rewritten to be short and plain: each row says what happened and “Next: …”. Statuses, consent and approvals are visible where the decision is made, and states cover empty, overdue, blocked and could-not-load.
rows.caption: Advocate · Overview

outcome.title: Safety first
outcome.text: A crisis notice on every screen, consent before every referral and separate consent for recording.

outcome.title: One design language
outcome.text: The approved Veteran panel set the style; Advocate and Partner follow the same shell and components.

outcome.title: Wired prototypes
outcome.text: Over 240 frames with numbered names and real links, so every button leads to a real screen.
